skill.name: managing-relationships
skill.description: Manage GitHub parent-child issue relationships, dependencies, and relationship queries with a helper script that uses the GitHub GraphQL API.
skill.summary: Manage GitHub issue hierarchies, dependency views, and relationship queries through GitHub GraphQL.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: The static command findings were adjudicated as safe documented usage or hardcoded GitHub CLI calls rather than hidden shell execution. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, obfuscation, or arbitrary command injection was found in SKILL.md or scripts/manage-relationships.py. The skill still performs authenticated GitHub issue mutations, so users should confirm relationship changes before execution.

remediation.issue: Authenticated GitHub mutations can change repository issue hierarchy.
remediation.suggestion: Prompt for confirmation before add, remove, or replace-parent operations, and show the target issue numbers first.

remediation.issue: Direct GraphQL examples allow broad GitHub API operations if copied without review.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer the bundled wrapper script for routine tasks and label raw GraphQL examples as advanced manual usage.

remediation.issue: GraphQL query strings are assembled manually in the helper script.
remediation.suggestion: Keep user inputs typed as integers and escape or validate any future free-text fields before adding them to queries.

content.value_statement: GitHub issue hierarchies are hard to manage with the standard issue CLI. This skill uses GraphQL workflows to add, remove, inspect, and verify issue relationships.
actual_capabilities: Add a GitHub issue as a sub-issue of another issue.
Remove a sub-issue from its parent issue.
List sub-issues, parents, and relationship summaries for an issue.
Show blocking and blocked-by dependencies for a GitHub issue.
Retrieve GitHub GraphQL node IDs from issue numbers.
Verify relationship changes after GitHub API operations.
limitations: Requires an authenticated GitHub CLI with GraphQL API access.
Works against the current repository context detected by the GitHub CLI.
Blocking relationships are shown by the script but not created by it.
Does not create issues, labels, milestones, or project fields by itself.

use_cases.title: Plan Epic Hierarchies
use_cases.description: Create clear parent-child structures for epics, features, and implementation tasks.

use_cases.title: Audit Issue Dependencies
use_cases.description: Review which issues are blocked, blocking, or tracked before a release decision.

use_cases.title: Maintain Repository Triage
use_cases.description: Move issues between parents and verify relationship changes during backlog cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: List Issue Relationships
prompt_templates.prompt: Show all relationships for issue 67 in the current GitHub repository.

prompt_templates.title: Add One Sub-Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Make issue 68 a sub-issue of issue 67, then verify the relationship.

prompt_templates.title: Build An Epic Tree
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a parent-child hierarchy where issue 1 contains issues 2 and 3, and issue 2 contains issues 5 and 6.

prompt_templates.title: Review Dependencies Before Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect issue 42, list its parent, sub-issues, blocked-by issues, and blocking issues, then summarize release risks.

output_examples.output: Issue 67 has three sub-issues: 68, 69, and 70. No parent issue was found. Issue 69 is blocked by issue 44.

output_examples.input: Make issue 68 a child of issue 67 and verify it.
output_examples.output: Issue 68 was added as a sub-issue of issue 67. Verification shows issue 68 in the sub-issue list for issue 67.

output_examples.input: Check dependencies for issue 12 before release.
output_examples.output: Issue 12 is blocked by issues 14 and 18. It blocks issue 31. Review the blockers before marking the release ready.

best_practices: Confirm parent and child issue numbers before running mutation commands.
Create all issues before adding parent-child relationships.
Verify relationship state after each mutation or batch operation.
anti_patterns: Do not use task list references when a true sub-issue relationship is required.
Do not move an issue to a new parent without checking its current parent first.
Do not build deep hierarchies that are hard to navigate in GitHub.

faq.question: Does this skill create GitHub issues?
faq.answer: No. It manages relationships between existing GitHub issues.

faq.question: What GitHub access is required?
faq.answer: It requires an authenticated GitHub CLI with permission to read and update issues in the repository.

faq.question: Can one issue have multiple parents?
faq.answer: No. GitHub sub-issues allow one parent per issue.

faq.question: Can it create blocking dependencies?
faq.answer: The script can show blocking relationships, but the documented implementation does not create them.

faq.question: Does it work outside the current repository?
faq.answer: The script detects the current repository through the GitHub CLI and works in that context.

faq.question: Should mutation commands be confirmed first?
faq.answer: Yes. Review issue numbers and intended changes before running commands that alter relationships.
